textbookText: Example: 1. In red deer, old female (hind) is the leader who looks after the welfare of other females and young ones. Male deer (Stag) only visits the herd at the time of breeding season for mating. Later the stag moves away. 2. Sometimes, a flock of geese can be seen flying over the sky, in which a bird at the front is leading the flock. 3. In honey bee colony, all the activities of beehive are regulated and co-ordinated by a queen bee with the help of pheromones. 4. In the rhesus monkey, leadership and dominance are found together in which wide range of territory is maintained by a strong and aggressive dominant male as a leader in the troop. A troop consists of less dominant adult males, adult females and infants.

Let’s discuss some questions before starting this topic: i. What do you mean by migration? ii. Do all animals migrate? iii. What might be the causes of migration in animals? iv. Have you ever seen bird migration in the sky?

The term migration is derived from a Latin word ‘Migrare’ which literally means ‘to travel or going from one place to another’. Migration is the regular and periodic passing of animals from one place to another place for various purposes. It is a complex type of inborn behaviour which is shown by insects, birds fishes, some mammals, turtle etc. Animals migrate for various purposes viz. in search of food, to protect from adverse environmental condition, to find mate, shelter and for reproduction.

1. MIGRATION IN FISHES Migration in fishes can be defined as the to and fro movement from feeding and resting place to nesting and breeding place and vice versa. Not all fishes are migratory in nature and some fishes which don’t migrate at all are called resident fishes. Some fishes migrate daily and some fishes migrate at the specific time in the year. The distance of migration ranges from few meters to thousands of kilometer.

Fishes move by different ways during migration. For instance: some fish passively move with water current which is called drifting movement and some migrating fishes swim in all directions called random swimming movement. Another type of movement in fishes in which they swim in the particular direction in response to the certain stimulus is called oriented swimming movement.
